title.title: A finite lattice that is no finite algebra's congruence lattice
title.subtitle: Claim: some finite lattice is not $\mathrm{Con}(A)$ for any finite algebra $A$; representability is undecidable

plain: Some finite 'family tree' of groupings can never come from any finite algebra

beats.text: A finite lattice, drawn small and schematically; the paper's obstruction is much larger
Every algebraic lattice is a congruence lattice, if infinite algebras are allowed
With finite algebras, the claim is no, and recognizing which lattices work is undecidable

steps: Turn the question into a colouring test on graphs
Run finite lattices through the test
One lattice fails: no finite algebra has it

data.label: fails the test
data.caption: finite lattices through the colouring test

achievement.label: Finite lattice representation problem (after 1963)
statement: \exists\, L \text{ finite}: \; L \not\cong \mathrm{Con}(A) \text{ for every finite } A
achievement.context: Equivalently (Pálfy–Pudlák, 1980): a finite lattice that is no interval in a finite group's subgroup lattice
achievement.note: Plus a coloured-graph characterization; 267 pages over two papers

verify.detail: Lean has the coloured-graph characterization only, not the negative answer or undecidability
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Is every finite lattice the congruence lattice of a finite algebra? Open for decades.
A colouring test on graphs characterizes these lattices, and one lattice fails it.
Claimed: no, and it is undecidable.

sources.quote: Grätzer and Schmidt proved in 1963 that every algebraic lattice is the congruence lattice of some algebra.
Pálfy and Pudlák showed in 1980 that it is equivalent to every finite lattice being an interval in the subgroup lattice of a finite group.
The two papers come to 267 pages.
only the coloured-graph characterization equivalence (FiniteCongruenceGraph.lean) — the negative answer and undecidability are NOT formalized
